situation:
You are the human resources manager at RIDGELINE FREIGHT LINES, a regional trucking carrier that hauls refrigerated freight for grocery and food service customers. The chief operating officer (judge) has asked to meet with you about the driver referral bonus program and about a contract the sales team brought in last week.

RIDGELINE FREIGHT LINES is two years old and employs about 140 drivers. Most of them were recruited by other drivers through the referral program, which pays a bonus for every driver a current employee brings in who stays six months. When the program launched, management told the workforce in writing that every referral already in progress would be paid. The company is now spending the last of its first round of funding.

STONEGATE GROCERY DISTRIBUTORS has offered the carrier a dedicated regional contract that would steady revenue and strengthen the case for a second round of investment. It requires thirty more drivers seated within sixty days. Referrals cannot fill that many seats that fast. Signing bonuses paid to outside applicants could, but the only money available for them is the pool reserved for the referral bonuses drivers are already waiting on.

Moving that money would let the carrier take the contract, and it would tell the drivers who recruited their friends that a written commitment gives way when a customer is large enough; experienced drivers who leave over it are slow and costly to replace. Turning the contract down keeps the promise but leaves the company burning the last of its funding with no new revenue coming in.

The chief operating officer (judge) wants you to analyze the factors bearing on the decision, recommend what should happen to the referral bonus program, and explain how the decision would be communicated to the drivers. The chief operating officer (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the chief operating officer (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief operating officer (judge) at RIDGELINE FREIGHT LINES. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the human resources manager to recommend whether the referral bonus pool should be moved into signing bonuses for outside applicants so the carrier can seat thirty drivers for the STONEGATE GROCERY DISTRIBUTORS contract, or whether the written promise to the drivers should be kept and the contract turned down. You want the factors that bear on that choice, a recommendation, and a plan for telling the drivers.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would our drivers describe the way we handled this?
If we move this money once, what happens the next time a large customer asks?
